meeting_header: 2026-03-21 15:30 UTC · 55 minutes · Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Aegis VP Product), Ethan Cole (Aegis ML Eng), Maya Lin (Aegis Security), Aaron Patel (Aegis Infra)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Aegis HealthTech's clinical summarization and triage use cases. Main concerns: context length (single patient records up to ~80k tokens), multilingual support (EN + ES + PT), tool-calling to query internal FHIR DB, and compliance (SOC 2, KMS, VPC). Evaluating Hosted for fast start, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private for strict PHI controls. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot on Dedicated and follow with technical deep-dive on tool-calling and latency/cost tradeoffs.
topics: Open model comparisons (LLM families and quantization tradeoffs)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Multilingual model support and hallucination rates
Tool-calling / function calling to internal FHIR DB
Security: SOC 2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to learn about your use cases and constraints.
[00:08] Priya Sharma: Thanks, Sofia. Quick background - Aegis builds clinical summarization tools, we ingest EHR notes and need to generate patient summaries and triage suggestions. We're exploring which model & deployment fit best.
[00:22] Daniel Park: cool, are you mostly looking at hosted first or more of a private/dedicated long term?
[00:27] Ethan Cole: Long term we need PHI controls, probably Private, but we want to prototype quickly with Hosted or Dedicated to get baseline. latency and cost matter, but compliance is a hard req.
[00:40] Maya Lin: security wise we need SOC 2, SSO + SCIM, envelope encryption, and ideally HSM/KMS integration. Also gotta show audit logs for clinicians access.
[00:54] Sofia: absolutely; Redwood offers Hosted for fast start, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). We can do KMS integrations and audit logs - I'll share the security pack.
[01:06] Aaron Patel: Our main technical constraint: single patient bundles can be very long, sometimes up to 80k tokens after concatenation. We need model context >64k ideally 100k. How does that work w/ open models?
[01:20] Daniel: Great question. There are open models that support long context (some Llama-family variants, LongLoRA-style rehabs, some Mistral forks), but performance and cost differ. Redwood's runtime supports efficient KV cache management and quantized kernels to handle long sequences, but you'll want to pick a model architecture we've validated for 64k-100k.
[01:41] Priya: Are there big differences in hallucination for long context between the open models? We also need multilingual - English, Spanish, Portuguese.
[01:50] Daniel: Yes, multilingual pretraining matters. Some models degrade on non-English; model selection should include multilingual evals. For hallucinations, model family + prompting & tool-calling (retrieval or DB calls) reduces hallucinations.
[02:04] Ethan: We plan to do tool-calling: when model needs a medication list or lab history, it should call a function that queries our FHIR DB. Do you support function/tool calling?
[02:12] Sofia: yes, Redwood supports function calling/tool invocation patterns - note transcription sometimes calls it tool-calling. There's streaming and structured output support; SEs can help wire up auth for internal APIs.
[02:23] Daniel: For latency, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency vs Hosted at scale since you're on reserved GPUs. Hosted is great for evaluation and early prod but if you need SLOs and predictable perf for triage (sub-second token latency targets) Dedicated or Private is better.
[02:40] Priya: Cost vs latency tradeoffs - we care about per-request cost but also clinician experience. What's the typical per-token difference between Hosted and Dedicated for quantized open models?
[02:51] Daniel: It varies a lot: Dedicated can be 30-60% cheaper at scale because you amortize GPU costs and we can use optimized kernels + batching. Quantized FP16/INT8 models further reduce cost. We'll include model-level perf numbers in the pricing sheet.
[03:07] Maya: For Private deployment, how isolated is the control plane? We have enterprise legal wanting customer-managed networking.
[03:13] Sofia: Private gives a customer-managed VPC option; the control plane can be on-prem or in your cloud, and we integrate with your KMS/HSM. We'll share the architecture doc.
[03:23] Ethan: For the pilot, we want to test 64k and 100k context models, check latency on our prompts, and validate tool-calling integration. Can Redwood spin up a Dedicated pilot with 2x A100 equivalence?
[03:34] Sofia: yes, we can propose a pilot config: Dedicated pool with reserved capacity, pre-installed model variants (64k/100k) and access to a sandbox tool-calling endpoint. We'll send an agreement.
[03:44] Aaron: Any caveats around quantized models and tool-calling or function outputs being stable? We've seen some differences in outputs between FP16 and INT8.
[03:52] Daniel: Good point - quantization can slightly change tokenization behavior and logits, which occasionally impacts structured outputs. We recommend running the exact output tests you need; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles that preserve function-calling fidelity.
[04:07] Priya: On multilingual, we need quality parity across EN/ES/PT for summaries. How do you evaluate that?
[04:14] Daniel: We run parallel evals on representative prompt sets, sample F1/ROUGE-ish metrics where applicable and human sampling. We'll do a multilingual pilot subset.
[04:25] Priya: Any competitors we should be looking at?
[04:28] Sofia: Customers often compare OpenAI (hosted), Anthropic, Cohere, and some self-host like Replicate - each has tradeoffs on governance, pricing, and context size.
[04:39] Maya: We need to get legal and security comfortable - so security docs, SOC2, data residency notes, and SAML/SSO details please.
[04:48] Sofia: noted - Daniel will send the security pack; I'll follow up with pricing and pilot contract.
[04:55] Ethan: timeline wise, if we do pilot next week, how long to stand up environment?
[04:59] Daniel: We can provision Dedicated pilot in 2-3 business days once contract is signed; Private on prem will take longer.
[05:06] Sofia: recap: Redwood to send pricing + pilot agreement, security + KMS docs, and SE to run technical deep-dive on tool-calling next Tue. Aegis to share prompt samples and target evaluation criteria.
[05:16] Priya: sounds good. Thanks all.
[05:18] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with meeting notes and next steps.
